title: Contrast for Interface Parts
context: Non-text contrast for inputs, borders, icons, and charts
whyItMatters: Text is not the only part of an interface that needs to be visible. Boundaries help people find controls and distinguish chart information.
learningObjectives: Understand the 3:1 target for borders and icons.
Apply contrast ideas to data visualizations.
lessonParagraphs: Buttons, text input borders, icons, and chart elements are interface components without words. They need a clear boundary so people can see where to interact.

A faint field border can blend into its background. The research gives a 3:1 target for non-text graphical components against adjacent colors. Avene currently focuses on text contrast, so this topic is outside its detection scope.
Adjacent colors in a pie chart can blend together. The research suggests using distinct lightness or adding a dark border between slices.
A visible cue can also communicate a component boundary. For example, a button without a border may still be clear if its text signals its purpose.
keyTakeaways: Icons, borders, and input fields need a visible boundary.
The research gives a 3:1 target for non-text components.
Other cues can help distinguish chart elements and controls.
reviewFlags: The overview lists 4 minutes, while the detailed reading, video, and quiz budget totals 4.5 minutes.
internalNote: This topic is outside the scope of Avene's text-only detection engine.
